name: chain-of-thought
context: Tasks where the model must reason through multiple intermediate steps before producing a final answer; foundational prompt-level scaffolding for all structured reasoning patterns.
benefits: Makes the reasoning trace inspectable and auditable
No extra tools or LLM calls required
Composes with every other agent pattern
tradeoffs: Chains can be plausible but wrong
Can decrease accuracy on easy questions by introducing plausible-but-wrong reasoning variability
anti_patterns: Hiding the reasoning chain from logs
Adding explicit CoT to reasoning models on simple tasks causes overthinking and wastes tokens
design_principles: Externalize intermediate steps before the answer
Keep chain structure consistent across calls
best_practices: Provide few-shot examples of good chains
Combine with structured-output for machine-readable steps
Use self-consistency (k=5, majority vote) for high-stakes math/logic; vote on answers not traces
Separate reasoning in dedicated field (e.g., reasoning + answer schema) for parseable audit traces
references: Wei et al., Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models, 2022 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11903
